title: Everything Bagel Leaders
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece names and critiques a leadership pattern the author calls the 'Everything Bagel Leader' — someone who says yes to every initiative and passes the resulting overload onto their team. It diagnoses the motivations behind the pattern, from fear of missing out to a desire to impress superiors, and describes the burnout and exhaustion that results when priorities never get trimmed. The article then flips perspective to the team's coping strategies, noting that team members often have to quietly re-prioritize their leader's commitments themselves, asking forgiveness rather than permission. The closing argument is a call for ruthless prioritization: turning ten priorities into three as a survival skill for teams stuck under this kind of leader.
points: The essay names a specific and recognizable dysfunction — a leader who cannot say no — and traces it to two root motivations: FOMO and a desire to impress superiors.
It documents an underground coping mechanism: team members re-prioritizing their leader's commitments without permission because the leader won't do it themselves.
The piece frames constant new initiatives (via books, podcasts, social media) as making the overload worse, not better, despite good intentions.
Its actionable takeaway — 'turning 10 priorities into three' — is a concrete prioritization heuristic rather than a vague call for balance.
quotes: Their inability to say No creates an unnecessary burden on the team that often leads to exhaustion, frazzle, and burnout.
There is nothing worth saying No to if you’re an Everything Bagel Leader. Ideas and projects arrive in a never-ending wave.
The Everything Bagel Leader will never accept this re-prioritization, so team members ask for forgiveness later rather than permission, as the saying goes.
A leader who always says Yes can be a curse for a productive team.
Turning 10 priorities into three is how good team members survive.
